title: Royal Pancake Day Announcement
text:
Hear ye, hear ye! By order of Queen Maple the Kind, tomorrow is Royal Pancake Day in the Kingdom of Oatmeadow. All {plural noun} must be washed and set out on the castle steps by seven in the morning.

The royal chef will make one giant pancake as big as a {noun}. It will be topped with honey, berries, and a spoonful of {food}. The queen asks that everyone eat {adverb} and say thank you to the cook.

After breakfast, the royal band will play a {adjective} song while the king tries to {verb} on one foot. Last year he {past tense verb} right into the fountain, so please stand back.

Children may bring their pet {animal} to the parade, but please keep it on a leash. Anyone who sees the royal cat {verb ending in ing} on the throne again should ring the {adjective} bell and shout, "{exclamation}!" Thank you, and long live the {plural noun}!

title: My Week as the Castle Mail Carrier
text:
Monday: Today was my first day as the castle mail carrier! I got a {adjective} hat and a bag full of {plural noun}. The castle has two hundred stairs, so I walked {adverb} all the way to the top of the tower.

Tuesday: The king got a letter from his cousin. It smelled like {food} and was tied with a {noun}. He read it three times and then {past tense verb} for the rest of the afternoon.

Wednesday: The queen ordered {number} boxes of {plural noun} for the garden. They were very heavy, so the castle goat helped me carry them. Behind the last box, I found the princess {verb ending in ing}. She said she was practicing for the talent show.

Friday: I got a letter of my very own! It said, "Thank you for being so {adjective}. Please come back next week and bring a {noun}." I can't wait to {verb} again on Monday.

title: Rules for Visiting Sunnyhill Castle
text:
Welcome to Sunnyhill Castle! Please follow these rules so everyone has a {adjective} visit. Rule one: Wipe your feet before you walk on the royal rug. The rug is three hundred years old and is made of {plural noun}.

Rule two: Do not {verb} in the throne room. The king is very {adjective} about his quiet time. If you must talk, please whisper {adverb}. Rule three: The castle cat, Sir Fluffington, may sleep anywhere he wants, even in the queen's {noun}. Do not wake him up, or he will meow for {number} hours.

Rule four: The moat is for ducks only. No swimming, no {verb ending in ing}, and no throwing {plural noun} into the water.

Thank you for visiting! On your way out, please stop by the gift shop and buy a {adjective} {noun}. The money helps us feed the royal {animal}.

title: The Prince's Birthday Feast Menu
text:
Tonight the castle celebrates the little prince's sixth birthday! To start, each guest will get a warm bowl of tomato soup with a {noun} floating in the middle. The soup will be served {adverb} by the royal chef, who is wearing her best {color} apron.

The main dish is roasted carrots, mashed potatoes, and a big pile of {plural noun}. The prince asked for extra {food} on the side, so there will be {number} buckets of it on every table.

For dessert, the bakers made a {adjective} cake shaped like a {noun}. It took them all week, and last night one baker {past tense verb} right into the frosting. When the candles are lit, everyone will sing and the prince will try to {verb} without laughing.

After the feast, guests may stay to dance. The queen says the dance floor is very {adjective}, so please wear {plural noun} on your feet. Happy birthday, Prince Teddy!

title: Help Wanted: Royal Pillow Fluffer
text:
HELP WANTED: The castle of King Barnaby is looking for a new Royal Pillow Fluffer. Our last pillow fluffer moved to the seaside to sell {plural noun}.

The king has {number} pillows on his bed, and every single one must be fluffed {adverb} each morning. Most of the pillows are filled with feathers. One pillow is filled with {food}. Nobody knows why.

The right person for this job should be {adjective}, patient, and good at {verb ending in ing}. You must be able to {verb} while carrying a tall stack of pillows up the stairs. Napping on the job is only allowed on Tuesdays.

You will get a room in the tower, a {adjective} uniform, and all the {plural noun} you can eat. To apply, please send a letter to the castle and tell us about a time you {past tense verb} with a pillow. Please include a drawing of your favorite {noun}.

title: Meet the Castle Gardener
text:
This week, the Oatmeadow Gazette visited Mr. Hobbs, who has been the castle gardener for forty years. We asked him about his favorite part of the job. "The roses," he said. "I water them every morning and sing them a {adjective} song. They grow best when I {verb} next to them."

Next we asked about the strangest thing he ever grew. "One spring, the queen gave me some seeds from far away," he said. "I planted them {adverb}, and they grew into a giant {noun}. Birds built {number} nests in it."

Mr. Hobbs also told us his secret for the best vegetables. "Every Tuesday, I feed the carrots a little bowl of {food}," he whispered. "And I never let the rabbits see me {verb ending in ing}."

At the end of our visit, Mr. Hobbs gave us a {adjective} pumpkin and a basket of {plural noun}. He waved {adverb} as we left. What a {adjective} man!

title: A Letter from Princess June
text:
Dear Pen Pal, hello from the castle! My name is Princess June, and I am seven years old. Thank you for your letter about your farm. Here is what life is like at my house.

Our castle has one hundred rooms, but my favorite is the kitchen. The cook lets me stir the soup and taste the {plural noun}. Yesterday we made muffins with {food} inside, and they were very {adjective}.

My brother and I have a pet {animal} named Duke. He sleeps in a {noun} by the fireplace and snores {adverb}. Every night, he {past tense verb} up the stairs to say goodnight to the guards.

This weekend my family is going to {verb} at the lake. My dad, the king, says I can bring my {adjective} kite and {number} friends. Do you want to come? Please write back soon and tell me all about your {plural noun}.

Your friend,
Princess June

title: The Royal Lost and Found
text:
The castle Lost and Found is getting very full! If any of these things belong to you, please come to the front gate and talk to Gerald.

Found in the throne room: one {adjective} crown, two left shoes, and a jar of {plural noun}. The jar has a note on it that says "Do not open until Tuesday." Found in the royal garden: a {noun} with the queen's name on it. The queen says she has never seen it before. It was found {verb ending in ing} under the apple tree.

Found in the kitchen: {number} wooden spoons and a {color} sock. The cook says the sock is not hers, but it smells a little like {food}. Found in the tower: a book called How to {verb} Like a King. Someone has read it very {adverb}.

If nobody picks up these things by Friday, Gerald will give them to the royal goat. Last week the goat {past tense verb} a whole box of hats. Thank you, and please remember to label your {plural noun}!

title: Castle News: The King's New Hat
text:
Good evening, and welcome to Castle News. Our top story tonight: King Barnaby has a new hat! The hat arrived this morning in a box as big as a {noun}. It is tall, shiny, and covered in {plural noun}. The king put it on {adverb} and looked in the mirror for {number} minutes.

People all over the kingdom came to see it. A farmer said it looked like a {adjective} {food}. One little girl said the hat made her want to {verb}. The royal dog {past tense verb} at it and then hid under the table.

There was only one problem. The hat was so tall that the king could not fit through the door. He spent the whole afternoon {verb ending in ing} in the hallway. The castle builders are now making the door a little bit more {adjective}.

That is all for tonight. Tomorrow we will report on the queen's {adjective} new shoes. Good night, and sleep {adverb}!

title: The Big Castle Sleepover Plan
text:
The prince is having a sleepover at the castle this Saturday! At six o'clock, guests will arrive at the front gate. Please bring a sleeping bag, a toothbrush, and your favorite {noun}. The guards will help carry your {plural noun} up to the tower.

At seven o'clock, we will eat pizza in the great hall. The royal cook will put {food} on top, because that is what the prince likes best. After dinner, everyone will play a game called Hide and {verb}. Last time, the king hid inside a {noun} and {past tense verb} until breakfast.

At eight o'clock, the queen will read a {adjective} story by the fire. Please sit {adverb} and keep your feet off the royal pillows.

At nine o'clock, it is lights out. If you hear something {verb ending in ing} in the hallway, do not worry. It is just the royal cat. Sweet dreams, and say goodnight to the {adjective} moon!
